cover.caption: Kona skulle ut og leie seg en gjeter.
cover.alt: Kona står på stien ved skogkanten med staven sin. Foran henne står bjørnen med gjeterstav og veske, ulven og reven på rad, og alle vil bli gjeter.

Create the cover illustration for an illustrated folk-tale book, in a square format. Do not write a title or any other text on it.

Picture: On the grassy track at the edge of the birch forest on a clear, cool morning, the Farm Wife leans on her birch stick and sizes up three would-be herdsmen lined up on the verge: the Bear standing upright with his shepherd's crook and leather bag, the Wolf trying his best to look polite, and the Fox sitting neatly with his black-tipped tail around his paws, smiling sweetly. Red dwarf birch and golden grass line the track, with blue ridges far away.

Characters in this picture (nobody else, unless the picture description mentions them):
- the Farm Wife: A strong, broad-shouldered farm woman of about forty with a wide, sun-browned face, a broad nose, sharp blue eyes under straight black eyebrows and a firm, no-nonsense mouth; her black hair is tucked under a dark-red kerchief knotted at the nape. She wears a dark-green wool dress with rolled-up sleeves, a blue-and-white checked apron, a wide leather belt and sturdy leather shoes, and carries a long, white-barked birch stick.
- the Bear: A huge bear with thick, shaggy honey-blond fur, paler cream fur on his muzzle and belly, a wide round face, small half-moon ears, a shiny black nose, small kind brown eyes and a tuft of fur sticking up on top of his head. He stands upright on his hind legs like a man and carries a long wooden shepherd's crook and a worn leather shoulder bag.
- the Wolf: A lanky, long-legged grey wolf with shaggy smoke-grey fur, darker along his back and pale silver on his chest and legs, a long, narrow muzzle, pale yellow eyes, tall pointed ears with the left one bent over at the tip, and a thin bushy tail held low. He wears a polite, awkward, closed-mouth smile and looks gangly rather than fierce.
- the Fox: A fox with glossy golden-orange fur the colour of marigolds, a creamy-white bib and cheeks, dark-brown lower legs and feet, big ears lined with cream fur, large, round honey-brown eyes with an innocent look, a short muzzle and a sweet smile. His full, fluffy golden-orange tail has a sooty black end. A thin strap across his breast holds a little brown leather shepherd's pouch.

Story world: Old rural Norway, where the animals can talk. The woman keeps her animals at a mountain summer farm high up where the birch forest ends: a small grey log hut with a turf roof and a stone doorstep, a little cowshed and a split-rail fence around a green pasture, with a stony stream below and a grove of birches beyond it. A grassy track leads from the pasture down into the birch forest. Her butter churn is a tall, narrow wooden churn with dark hoops and a long wooden dasher sticking out of its lid. The wolf and the fox look like real animals, apart from the fox's little pouch; the bear walks upright with a crook and a bag.

This story's season, light and colours: Late August at a mountain summer farm, when the fells take on their first autumn colours: deep-red dwarf birch and golden grass on the slopes, ripe blueberries, blue ridges far away and clear, cool air. The evening glows orange and rose over the mountains. Accents: dwarf-birch red, the fox's golden orange and the white of the cream.

Art style: Classic Norwegian folk-tale book illustration: fine pen-and-ink line work with transparent watercolour washes on warm, slightly textured off-white paper, in the tradition of 19th-century Scandinavian book illustration, like the plates of an old printed book of folk tales, with a deep red that comes back as the accent. The picture fills the whole image, with no border, frame or lettering. Naturalistic proportions and expressive, characterful faces; every character has their own face, build, age and hair exactly as described, so no two characters look alike. Muted natural palette of fjord teal, slate blue, moss green, lichen grey, honey ochre, lingonberry red, ink black and birch white, shifted towards each story's own season, light and colours, with the warm cream paper showing through the washes, with dramatic Nordic light: low sun, long shadows, blue dusk and firelight. Old rural Norway: dark spruce and pine forests, steep mountains, fjords, turf-roofed log farms, carved wood, homespun wool and linen. Trolls are enormous, ancient and earthy, like pieces of the landscape come alive, made of moss, bark, stone and lichen, and more grotesque-comic than frightening. Kings and princesses wear modest medieval finery. Careful composition with depth and atmosphere, one clear focal point and room for the landscape. Not cute or cartoonish, not photorealistic, not 3D, not anime, no glossy digital look.

Rules:
- No text of any kind: no letters, words, numbers, signatures, captions, speech bubbles or logos.
- Every named character must match their model sheet and description exactly: the same face, hair, colours, clothes and proportions.
- Suitable for readers of all ages: no blood, wounds or gore, and no killing shown. Show danger and cruelty through atmosphere, posture and suspense, never through injury.
- Draw each named character only once.
- Show exactly the number of people, animals and things the description asks for, and no extra people.
- One clear moment that reads at a glance, as a single full-bleed picture with no border, frame or comic panels.

illustrations.anchor: Da kona kom tilbake og så det, ble hun så sint
illustrations.caption: Den siste skvetten fløte traff reven ytterst på halen.
illustrations.alt: Kona står sint ved smørkjerna utenfor seterbua og slenger den siste fløten etter reven. Den treffer ham ytterst på halen idet han springer sin vei.
